Chapter 06 of 19

The Old Line

BroadcastCommercial Drive / erased rail routes100 BPM
The story

Terminal City does not abandon routes. It only takes them off the public schedule. Under Commercial Drive and the streets around it, old streetcar rails still lie beneath the asphalt, and on wet nights they come back. Look at the reflections in a puddle and you might see them, shining where no track should be.

Sometimes a car arrives on the Old Line. It has no route number and no destination sign. It stops where work needs doing, not where the passengers would like to go. You may board. You may not choose where you get off. The Repair People's marks show which stops are safe, and the crows ride short sections when their wings are tired.

The Old Line is the older relative of the SkyTrain, and it carries whatever the SkyTrain will not. The two lines do not speak to each other. Old line, still running. No request. Work ahead.

Terminal City is an original fictional mythology inspired by Vancouver’s geography, weather, wildlife, infrastructure, art, and electronic music. It makes no claim to historical, Indigenous, or religious tradition. Real places are used as settings; the operating system layered on them is invented. Photograph reality. Alter the evidence. Never illustrate the whole myth.
